thread.title: Trump Administration Moves to Dismiss Idaho Emergency Abortion Case
thread.title_full: Trump Administration Moves to Dismiss Idaho Emergency Abortion Case

author: LINDSAY WHITEHURST and REBECCA BOONE
title: Trump Administration Moves to Dismiss Idaho Emergency Abortion Case
text:
• The Trump administration filed a motion to dismiss an Idaho emergency abortion case on March 5, 2025.
• The lawsuit was originally filed by the Biden administration.
• The motion allows Idaho to enforce its strict abortion ban during emergency situations.
• A judge blocked the enforcement after doctors expressed concerns about airlifting women to other states for critical care.
• The Biden administration argued that emergency-room doctors must provide terminations to stabilize pregnant women.
• Idaho has one of the strictest abortion bans in the U.S.
• The case could have nationwide implications, as similar guidance was given to hospitals by the Biden administration after the Supreme Court's 2022 decision overturning Roe v. Wade.
• Idaho's state law allows lifesaving abortions, but the Biden administration's interpretation of federal law is contested.
• Doctors in Idaho report uncertainty in emergencies regarding the legality of performing abortions.
• St. Luke's Health System airlifted six patients out of state for medical emergencies during the ban from January to April 2024.
• Complaints about pregnant women being turned away from emergency rooms increased after the overturning of Roe v. Wade.
• Donald Trump appointed many Supreme Court justices who voted to overturn the constitutional right to abortion.
• Kelsey Pritchard from Susan B. Anthony Pro-Life America called the dismissal a win for women and unborn children.
• The Supreme Court previously ruled on the Idaho case, allowing hospitals to make determinations about emergency pregnancy terminations.
• The case is pending a ruling from the 9th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals.
• Brittany Fonteno from the National Abortion Federation criticized the administration's decision to withdraw from the case.
• Approximately 50,000 people in the U.S. develop life-threatening pregnancy complications each year.
• Currently, 12 states enforce bans on abortion at all stages of pregnancy, with limited exceptions.
